requirements.evidence: Several files cannot load: app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:44,56,73 return redirects from methods declared ': void' (compile-time fatal); app/Models/EntityMembership.php:7,9 imports BelongsTo twice (fatal); database/migrations/..._create_entity_memberships_table.php:22 uses ''owner'' inside a single-quoted PHP string (parse error), and the generated column is not STORED. app/Models/Entity.php:5-6,12-13 uses non-existent '#[HasFactory]'/'#[SoftDeletes]' attributes in place of the traits, so there are no soft deletes or factory; owner() at :40 declares HasOneThrough but returns HasOne. 'role' is cast to UserRole, but the code compares it to strings ('$membership->role === UserRole::Owner->value' in Members.php:60, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:26, and Settings.php:62), so the owner can be removed and transfer always returns 403. The last-manager check (Members.php:64) counts managers even when the member being removed is an employee. The 'Transferir propriedade' lang key is missing, and the views hard-code 'Transfer Ownership'. The EntityMembershipFactory (:23) only sets entity_id/user_id in afterCreating, after the NOT NULL insert has already run.

conventions.evidence: No app/Actions classes for domain writes: Members.php:36 and Settings.php:40,51,70 write directly from the components. Settings validates inline instead of using #[Validate] (Settings.php:36-39). The migrations have hand-picked timestamps. The views use no Bulma classes and hard-code English strings ('Add', 'Make Admin', 'Delete Entity', 'Name:'). Routes use Route::get instead of the sibling Route::livewire (routes/web.php:27-29). The change adds an AuthServiceProvider and a config/app.php providers array, which are legacy patterns. CHANGELOG.md is not updated. Entity pick authorizes by hand instead of through a policy.

security.evidence: Members::addMember (Members.php:28) never authorizes, so any member, including an employee, can add users. Settings save/delete/transfer (Settings.php:34,47,59) do no per-action authorize, so the owner check exists only at mount (a former owner keeps access in an open tab after a transfer). The enum-vs-string comparisons disable the owner guard in EntityMembershipPolicy::delete (:26) and removeMember (:60), so an admin can delete the owner's membership. assignRole (:43) can demote the owner to admin or employee, which leaves the entity with no owner. Models use '$guarded = []'.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: nothing under tests/, no unauthorized-call tests and no tamper tests, which the conventions require for every Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: The unneeded AuthServiceProvider and the rewritten provider/alias list in config/app.php:21-85 add code with no purpose here. Role arrays are rebuilt by hand in several places when the scopes already exist (EntityPolicy.php:14-16, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:18-20). There is also the array_map over manageable() in Members.php:45. Membership checks are duplicated across both policies.

readability.evidence: Unused imports: Auth in Members.php; User, Redirect and Log in Settings.php; Authenticatable in EntityController. Unused variable '$userId' at Settings.php:49. Settings.php:22-23 has misaligned indentation, and the Blade files have no trailing newline.

scope.evidence: config/app.php is rewritten: all comments are stripped, and the change adds a 'providers' array (naming EventServiceProvider and RouteServiceProvider, which are not in the diff) and an 'aliases' array with bogus facades ('Eloquent', 'Str' as a facade). This is unrelated to the task and likely breaks the app. The schema doc also drops the owner_membership_id and locale_default columns.

issues.explanation: save(), delete() and transfer() are declared ': void' but return redirect(), which is a PHP compile-time fatal error, so the Settings component cannot load.
''owner'' inside a single-quoted PHP string ends the literal and causes a parse error; the generated column is also not STORED as the task requires.
BelongsTo is imported twice, a fatal 'name already in use' error that prevents the model from loading.
#[HasFactory]/#[SoftDeletes] are not attributes, so the entity has neither soft deletes nor a factory; owner() at :40 declares a return type of HasOneThrough but returns HasOne.

role is cast to the UserRole enum, so comparing it with UserRole::Owner->value is always false; the owner's membership can be deleted (also Members.php:60), and transfer always aborts 403 (Settings.php:62).
addMember() calls no authorize, so employees can add members, contrary to the task and the Livewire security policy.
save/delete/transfer do not re-authorize manageSettings per action, which rule 3 of the Livewire policy requires.
assignRole can change the owner's own membership to admin or employee, which leaves the entity with no owner.
The last-manager check counts all managers without checking whether the target is a manager, so removing an employee is wrongly forbidden when there is a single manager.
entity_id and user_id are only set in afterCreating, after the insert has already failed on the NOT NULL foreign keys.
No tests are included, despite the mandatory TDD rule and the required unauthorized-call and tamper tests.
An unrelated rewrite of the app config adds a legacy providers/aliases list that references providers that do not exist and invalid facades.
Domain writes (update, delete, transfer, add member, assign role) are done in components instead of app/Actions classes.
'Transfer Ownership' is hard-coded and the required lang key ('Transferir propriedade') is missing; other screen texts are hard-coded too.
Inline validation is used instead of #[Validate] properties, and name has no max length.
CHANGELOG is not updated, and the Bulma classes and Route::livewire sibling style are not followed.
There is an unused $userId, unused imports and misaligned property indentation.

review.summary: The change adds entity and membership models, policies, a pick controller and three Livewire pages, but several files cannot even load: void methods return values, there is a duplicate import, the migration string has a parse error, and fake trait attributes stand in for HasFactory/SoftDeletes. It also has serious authorization holes: addMember is unauthorized, settings actions are not re-authorized, and enum-vs-string comparisons disable the owner protections. It ships no tests and rewrites config/app.php for no reason; reject.
